kill_fact: No kill fact survived. The two loudest bear claims verify against primary sources but one of them has since been answered by the company on the record, and the valuation anchors are stale by a week in the bull's favour. (1) Cost-curve truth holds: the 96.8% cash margin is the company's own filed figure - $94.7 million of cash margin on $97.8 million of revenue in the second quarter of 2026 (5 August 2026 release and 6 August call) - and a royalty company has no all-in sustaining cost to check it against, so the record's rejection of the 102.85% deterministic proxy is right. (2) Reserve/contract truth holds on the numbers but not on the rhetoric: Agnico Eagle's own releases confirm 60,000-80,000 ounces lost in the second half of 2026 and up to approximately 150,000 ounces a year in 2027 and 2028, and OR quantified its own share on the 6 August call at roughly 3,500 ounces in 2026 and up to roughly 7,500 a year in 2027-2028, about 18,500 over three years - the same arithmetic the bear did. But the bear's claim that the five-year outlook 'does not survive the arithmetic' is now rebutted by a checkable reason: the 2030 outlook is a 2030 endpoint, and Barnat was always scheduled to be mined out by 2028 or 2029, so the hole sits in the path rather than in the endpoint. Management reconciled rather than repeated a reassurance, which is precisely the development the record itself listed as the one that would bring an entry forward. (3) Cyclical-peak cheapness is the one bear point that survives intact and gets worse: gold is $4,436.50 today against the record's $4,154 anchor, and 96.8 cents of every revenue dollar drops to cash, so the passing valuation guard is a metal-price print. At today's $33.54 the enterprise is about $6.43 billion against roughly $362 million of cash earnings - about 17.8 times, the same multiple the record measured, because price and earnings rose together. (4) No hidden disqualifier found: no reserve downgrade (Odyssey set a quarterly production record and the operator's stated life of mine runs decades out), no permit or licence issue, and the opposite of dilution - roughly 1.6 million shares bought back and cancelled year to date, including about 1.0 million for $29.1 million in July after the Barnat selloff, which fires the record's own 'is the buyback finally countercyclical' test in the company's favour. The fifth acquisition (Murray Brook, $28 million, closed July) was funded from cash, not equity, so the bear's stated confirming tripwire did not fire. The one structure worth naming is Amulsar, where OR's stream accrues but pays nothing until a $150 million Armenian government loan and OR's own loan are repaid - a disclosed subordination, and it carries almost no weight in the base case.
corrections: One load-bearing correction, plus two footnotes. MATERIAL: the base fair value is anchored to spot metal on 4 August ($4,150 gold) and the record says 95% of the value is the producing book, which converts metal price to cash roughly one-for-one. Gold is $4,436.50 on 11 August, 6.8% higher. Re-running the record's own schedule at today's spot: 92,000 gold-equivalent ounces at $4,436.50 is $408.2 million of revenue, a 97% cash margin leaves $395.9 million, less $34 million of corporate cash costs gives $361.9 million of cash earnings - which the chief financial officer independently corroborated on 6 August as 'close to USD 90 million per quarter' of adjusted earnings at current prices. At the record's own 19 times that is $6.88 billion, or $36.65 a share, plus $1.71 for development royalties and $0.80 for the investment portfolio, less $0.77 of net debt, and applying the record's own 2.2% discount step gives $37.50. FOOTNOTE 1: net debt as filed at 30 June 2026 is $143.7 million including finance leases, not the $139.4 million revolver-only figure the record uses - a $0.02 per share difference, and the record's direction and magnitude are right. FOOTNOTE 2: the record attributes the 'remediation complete in the third quarter, mining resumes in the fourth' timetable to Agnico Eagle's 2 July release; that release explicitly declined to give a timetable, and the schedule was published in Agnico Eagle's 29 July second-quarter results. The substance is correct, the date is not. NOTE ON THE CONCLUSION: the correction does not rescue the thesis. The shares are $33.54 today, not $31.19, so upside to the corrected fair value is 11.8% against the record's 12%, and downside to the unchanged $20 adverse case is 40%. The record's 'good business, fair price' verdict survives its own numbers being moved.

corrections_typed.basis: Spot gold is $4,436.50 on 11 Aug 2026 (FMP commodities quote) vs the $4,150 the record used as of 4 Aug; re-running the record's own schedule - 92,000 GEOs x $4,436.50 = $408.2m revenue, x97% cash margin = $395.9m, less $34m corporate = $361.9m cash earnings (corroborated by the CFO's 'close to USD 90 million per quarter' on the 6 Aug 2026 call), x19 = $6.88bn / 187.6m shares = $36.65, +$1.71 development royalties +$0.80 portfolio -$0.77 net debt ($143.7m as filed 5 Aug 2026), x the record's own 0.978 discount step = $37.50.
